title: Trouble With Making Variables Work For Me

posts.author: Reverend_Blackstar
posts.body:
I'm currently working through Beginning RPG Maker MV and I'm stuck on a relatively simple exercise. I am attempting to create a treasure chest that appears when I trigger enough trees linked to it.
Code for the trees is as follows:
Text  :  None,  Window,  Bottom
:        : This tree looks peculiar
If  :  Self Switch A is OFF
Control Variables  :  #0001  Tree  +=  1
Control Self Switch  :  A  =  ON
:  End
I have the Priority set on "
Same as characters
", the Trigger set on "
Action button
" and the Self-Switch A check turned on under Variables.
After that, I did a Quick Event Creation to make the chest and clicked on the Variable condition of "
0001  Tree  > 5
"
Yet, no matter how much I reenter the programming in the trees or for the chest (including full deletion and retyping of the tree code as well as recreating the chest via Quick Event Creation) it's refusing to appear whenever I've hit enough trees.
In short, HELP!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Reverend_Blackstar said:
the Trigger set on "
Action button
" and the Self-Switch A check turned on under Variables.
Click to expand...
I presume you are talking about the event page conditions, in which case the page conditions are what needs to be met for the event page to become active.
According to the event snippet you posted, you don't need to enable event page conditions at all because the event command:
"if self switch A is off" is handling the "do this thing once" part of the event.
As you can see, if the self switch is off, then it will do the thing then enable self switch A. From that point forward, self switch A is on, so "if self switch A is off" will never be met, and therefore it won't trigger that portion of the event.
If this is incorrect, then you will need to post a screenshot of your event so we can better see how you have created the event.

posts.author: Artille
posts.body:
Additionnaly to what has been said above, checking if self switch is set to OFF is a bit redundend (in this scenario).
By default, it is always OFF, meaning you can just skip that part of the code.
It can be usefull in certain conditions, especially when you are going back and forth with the selfswitches, but here it's a matter of "execute this event once".
You can rewrite it as such :
◆Text：None, Window, Bottom
：Text：This tree looks peculiar
◆Control Variables：#0001 Tree  +=  1
◆Erase Event
If you need that tree to be definitely put off (meaning, during the entire game), you can use the selfswitch with a second event page.
Instead of
Erase Event
, you want to set
selfswitch A
to
ON
Then, create a
new event page
, set the
conditions
to
self switch A
, and leave the page blank.
To achieve desired result and using this logic, you will need to duplicate this event 5 times, so that the player cuts down 5 trees, resulting in the variable value being 5.
Which should then trigger your chest to appear.
If you ever doubt of the actual variable value, you can use a seperate event with a character, use the text command and make him say something like :
Current variable value for Tree is : \v[1]
You will be able to see if it actually progress or not, enabling you to better target where the issue is.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body: Yes, if you're trying to activate from an adjacent tile, they need to be Same as Characters.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
As Zia mentioned, the event needs to be set to "same as player" in it's priority in order to be activated from an adjacent tile.
When the priority is set to below or above player, the player must be in the same grid in order to activate it.
